title: Payer/plan details
one_line_definition: This table compares year-over-year risk adjustment performance metrics across payers and their individual plans, covering membership size, documented and potential RAF risk, cost, and recapture effectiveness.
result_meaning: Analysts use this table to identify which payers and plans are improving or lagging in closing HCC coding gaps, capturing risk revenue, and managing cost trends relative to the prior year.

#Members.definition: The total count of enrolled members attributed to each payer or plan during the measurement period.
#Members.increasing: Rising membership may indicate plan growth, which can dilute or amplify risk scores and recapture rates depending on the health acuity of new enrollees.
#Members.decreasing: Falling membership may signal plan attrition or disenrollment, potentially skewing per-member metrics and reducing the absolute revenue opportunity for risk capture.

Documented risk.definition: The aggregate RAF score derived solely from HCC conditions that have already been coded and submitted for the current measurement period.
Documented risk.increasing: Higher documented risk reflects more thorough or complete coding of chronic and complex conditions, supporting stronger risk-adjusted revenue.
Documented risk.decreasing: Lower documented risk suggests coding gaps are widening or previously captured conditions are not being recaptured, threatening revenue adequacy.

Gap to potential risk.definition: The difference between a member's estimated maximum achievable RAF score and their currently documented RAF score, representing uncaptured coding opportunity.
Gap to potential risk.increasing: A growing gap indicates that more conditions are going uncoded relative to clinical evidence, signaling deteriorating documentation or care gap closure performance.
Gap to potential risk.decreasing: A shrinking gap means the plan is successfully identifying and closing HCC coding opportunities, moving documented risk closer to the clinically supported potential.

PMPM.definition: The average medical cost or premium revenue expressed on a per-member-per-month basis for each payer or plan.
PMPM.increasing: Rising PMPM may reflect higher-acuity membership, increased utilization, or cost trend acceleration, warranting review of care management interventions.
PMPM.decreasing: Falling PMPM can indicate improved care management efficiency, healthier member mix, or successful cost containment programs.

RAF recapture rate.definition: The percentage of previously documented HCC conditions from a prior period that were successfully re-documented and submitted in the current period.
RAF recapture rate.increasing: A higher recapture rate means the plan is effectively re-coding chronic conditions year over year, preserving risk-adjusted revenue continuity.
RAF recapture rate.decreasing: A lower recapture rate signals that chronic conditions coded in prior years are not being reconfirmed, creating revenue leakage and potential audit risk.

RAF recapture rate YoY.definition: The year-over-year percentage change in the RAF recapture rate, showing whether the plan's ability to re-document prior HCCs is improving or declining.
RAF recapture rate YoY.increasing: A positive YoY change indicates the plan is getting better at sustaining chronic condition documentation across annual coding cycles.
RAF recapture rate YoY.decreasing: A negative YoY change flags a worsening trend in recapturing previously coded HCCs, which may require targeted outreach or provider education.

Risk recapture rate.definition: The percentage of total identified RAF risk gaps — both existing and new — that were successfully closed through coding or clinical documentation in the current period.
Risk recapture rate.increasing: A higher risk recapture rate reflects stronger gap closure performance across all opportunity types, maximizing risk-adjusted revenue potential.
Risk recapture rate.decreasing: A lower risk recapture rate indicates that identified coding opportunities are not being acted upon, leaving significant RAF value and revenue unrealized.

Risk recapture rate YoY.definition: The year-over-year percentage change in the overall risk recapture rate, measuring whether gap closure effectiveness is trending positively or negatively.
Risk recapture rate YoY.increasing: A positive YoY trend demonstrates that care management and coding programs are becoming more effective at converting identified gaps into documented risk.
Risk recapture rate YoY.decreasing: A negative YoY trend signals declining program effectiveness or growing complexity of remaining gaps, requiring strategic intervention to reverse the trajectory.
